description:
## Goal

After blocked-wait producer discovery becomes edge-triggered, prove that no production scheduling path still orders FactKey values by Debug text. Delete this ticket as superseded if the cutover removes every affected path; otherwise repair only the surviving semantic ordering defect.

## Current evidence

The pre-cutover DependencyIndex::unresolved path sorts waits by Debug-rendered FactKey. Several FactKey variants embed raw interned Ty identities, so that text is not a stable structural order. The same unresolved inventory currently feeds producer-poke scheduling, but fz-kdt.46 owns deletion of those normal-drive scans and poke loops. Building a general structural comparator before that deletion would invest in machinery for a path intended to disappear.

## Strategy and proof

1. Land fz-kdt.46.
2. Search every remaining normal-drive consumer of unresolved waits and FactKey ordering.
3. If only terminal diagnostic presentation remains, keep deterministic presentation isolated from execution order and close this ticket with the removal proof.
4. If a live scheduling consumer remains, add opposite-Ty-mint-order and display-collision regressions, then use an injective structural order whose compare(a,b) == Equal iff a == b.
5. Do not restore a global producer scan or sort.
6. Prove byte-identical artifacts, order-independent causal work, complete diagnostics, full tests, fixture matrix, formatting, and strict clippy.

The expected outcome is deletion, not a comparator.
title: Audit residual blocked-wait ordering after edge-triggered cutover
